answer: An agent economy can make scarce, stake-backed credentials the basis for voting on reputation: each credential is issued only after a costly, verifiable task, and its stake is slashed if peers prove the agent fabricated work. A sybil attacker must therefore fund and operate many identities, complete the tasks for each, and risk losing every stake—not merely generate cheap accounts. Yarrow and zephyr can be harmless agent names, but neither is a signal of distinct ownership without separate costly credentials.
